name: Guamo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Guamo attested only in a 1778 anonymous wordlist; no stress information exists

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid guam1236 'Guamo' and reference records 133218 (Anónimo 1928 [1778], listed by Glottolog as a wordlist) and 41201 (Adelaar & Muysken 2004); langdoc searches for Guamo/Guama/Guamontey/Wamo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive work at all (0 grammar/sketch/phonology entries); the only language-specific reference is the 1928 wordlist. Dialects listed: San José Guamo (sanj1287), Santa Rosa Guamo (sant1461).

sources.citation: Jahn, Alfredo. 1927. Los aborígenes del occidente de Venezuela: su historia, etnografía y afinidades lingüísticas. Caracas: Lit. y Tip. del Comercio.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only one passing ethnohistorical mention of 'la nación guagiba y guamo' (p. 270); no Guamo vocabulary or linguistic remarks.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center, pp. 149-150 (Guamo stock).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification only: Guamo stock with Santa Rosa and San José dialects (both from Anonymous 1928, pp. 382-392) plus unattested Guamontey, Dazaro, Tayaga etc; 13-word comparative list (putí/puté 'head', aufé/ufé 'tooth', tuxua/tuagin 'eye', kum 'water'). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Gilij, Felipe Salvador. 1965. Ensayo de historia americana, tomo III (trans. Antonio Tovar). Fuentes para la Historia Colonial de Venezuela 73. Caracas: Academia Nacional de la Historia. Cap. IV pp. 136-137, cap. V p. 141.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Same content as the 1782 original: 'Todas las palabras, exceptuadas quizá las de los guamos, terminan constantemente en vocal' (p. 136); 'Ninguna de las orinoquenses, excepto el guamo, tiene la f' (p. 137); 'El guamo parece un alemán' (p. 141). No stress rule.

sources.citation: Anónimo. 1928 [ms. copy dated Santa Fé de Bogotá 9 Dec. 1788; Glottolog dates the original 1778]. "Traduccion de algunas voces de la lengua Guama." In: Lenguas de América. Manuscritos de la Real Biblioteca, tomo I (Catálogo de la Real Biblioteca vol. VI). Madrid: Gráficas Reunidas, pp. 381-393.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement. It is a Spanish-Guama wordlist (~350 items, doublets for the pueblos of Santa Rosa/Masparro and San José/Santo Domingo) printed 'con la misma ortografia que estaban en el original'; the forms carry acute and circumflex accents (matá, Famú, Putí ó Puté, Scará, Guaté, Titicunté, Dipiâ, Pichê, Dufpâ, Matatújua) but no rule is stated. The collector's closing note (p. 393) says only that many words 'tienen la aspiracion en las narices ó garganta, y en sonsonetes, dejos ó movimientos.. sin ser posible descifrarlos sino a viva voz'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Guamo language' (en) and 'Idioma guamo' (es), reproducing the 1928 wordlist.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; reproduces the wordlist and notes Kaufman (1990) finds a Chapacuran connection convincing.

sources.citation: Colección Mutis (Instituto Colombiano de Antropología e Historia), 'Manuscrito 2917 BPRM — Lengua Guama', online diplomatic transcription and facsimile, Portada + fol. 1r-14v.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The manuscript behind the 1928 print; would let one verify the original accent marks (acute vs circumflex) folio by folio and check for any editorial note on orthography. No stress rule expected.

sources.citation: Gilij, Filippo Salvadore. 1782. Saggio di storia americana, tomo III: Della religione, e delle lingue degli Orinochesi. Roma: Perego. Libro III, cap. IV-V (pp. ~150-158).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Impressionistic remarks only: Guamo, unlike the Orinoco languages, has abundant f and its words perhaps do not end in vowels (cap. IV); 'Pare il Guamo un Tedesco' [the Guamo sounds like a German] in a passage on the 'accento Indiano' of each nation (cap. V, p. 158); Guamo has only the dialect 'quaquaro'.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (passages on Guamo/Otomaco and the Venezuelan Llanos).
